Hi Tom / FinBank security,

Thanks again for taking the time today — good conversation. Quick recap and the next steps we agreed on from the call: 

- Current ask: confirm Redwood's encryption posture (at-rest / in-transit) and options for customer-managed keys (CMEK) / HSM-backed key storage.
- Documentation requested: SOC 2 report status, GDPR/HIPAA posture, and a started vendor security questionnaire.
- Next steps: I will share a short KMS overview and our SOC 2 summary; Camila will follow up on CMEK/HSM details and sample architecture.

Short answers up front: 
- Encryption: all data stored by Redwood is encrypted at rest using AES-256. All network traffic is TLS 1.2+ in transit.
- Customer-managed keys: we support customer-managed keys (CMEK) on our Private offering (VPC/on-prem) and on Dedicated via integrations with major KMS providers. We also have an HSM-backed option for customers with FIPS/HSM requirements.

Attachments: redwood_kms_overview.pdf, SOC2-latest-summary.pdf (see attached).

Hi Tom — thanks for the questions, happy to expand. Below are concise answers and pointers; happy to run through in the deep-dive and populate the vendor questionnaire where helpful.

1) CMEK availability:
- Hosted (Redwood API): we do not enable customer-managed keys for the fully-managed hosted tier due to multi-tenant constraints. For customers requiring CMEK, we recommend Dedicated or Private deployments.
- Dedicated: supports CMEK integrations with cloud KMS providers (AWS KMS CMEK, Google Cloud KMS) — key material is customer-controlled and never exported by Redwood.
- Private: full support for customer-managed keys and on-prem HSM integrations.

2) HSM options:
- For Dedicated and Private we integrate with HSM-backed KMS (AWS CloudHSM, Azure Dedicated HSM) and can also support customer-provided HSMs in on-prem deployments.
- Hardware / certification: the managed HSM options we integrate with are FIPS 140-2/140-3 compliant; for FIPS 140-3 Level 3 specifics we can provide vendor certs during the deep-dive.

3) Key lifecycle & access controls:
- Key rotation: customers can configure rotation policies in their KMS; Redwood supports automatic rekeying and seamless key re-association for active workloads.
- Separation of duties: Redwood runtime does not store raw key material. Access to key configuration (not material) is limited to a small set of infra/service accounts; engineer access to key material is blocked. We use role-based access control and audit logging for all key operations.

4) Evidence & artifacts we can provide:
- SOC 2 Type II report summary (attached).
- KMS integration diagrams and sample config snippets (will attach redwood_cmek_policy.pdf).
- Audit log samples and how we surface them in Redwood Console for Dedicated/Private customers.

I've attached redwood_cmek_policy.pdf with architecture notes and sample IAM mappings. If you want, we can start filling the vendor questionnaire — I can take initial pass on the KMS/encryption sections and Camila/Marissa will review.
